events.title: v1.0.0 starts the tracked semantic-conventions history
events.detail: The changelog begins with the first OpenTelemetry Specification release. Earlier semantic-conventions work was not tracked in this repository’s release history.

events.title: Metric and attribute requirement levels become stable
events.detail: The requirement-level model for metrics and attributes is marked stable, establishing a second axis alongside convention-group maturity.

events.title: Semantic conventions split into a separate release stream
events.detail: v1.21.0 is the first semantic-conventions release separate from the OpenTelemetry Specification release train.

events.title: Structured deprecations and the resource-to-entity model arrive
events.detail: Deprecation metadata becomes structured in the model, and resource groups are renamed to entity groups. This is a tooling and schema-shape milestone as well as a content change.

events.title: Entity registry and stability policies are introduced
events.detail: The repository adds explicit support for an entity registry and entity stability policies, making the domain lifecycle more machine-readable.

events.title: Deployment environment and telemetry distro entities reach stable
events.detail: deployment.environment.name, telemetry.distro.name, telemetry.distro.version, and the telemetry distro entity are promoted to stable.

events.title: Generic signal requirement-level documentation replaces metric-specific guidance
events.detail: The release consolidates requirement-level documentation around generic signal conventions and deprecates the older metric-specific documentation pattern.

events.title: Core HTTP semantic conventions stabilize
events.detail: v1.23.0 is called out as the first release where the core HTTP semantic conventions stabilized. Several requirements also become opt-in to control instrumentation cost.

events.title: Legacy HTTP attributes enter the deprecation list
events.detail: v1.24.0 adds http.flavor and http.user_agent to the list of deprecated attributes. This records the list update, not a claim that the stable HTTP domain was deprecated.

events.title: Core database conventions reach release candidate
events.detail: Database semantic conventions are promoted to release candidate, a major step toward the database core stabilization that is explicitly recognized in v1.33.0.

events.title: The database core stabilizes
events.detail: The release notes call this the first release where the core of database semantic conventions has stabilized; selected systems, including MariaDB, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, are stable.

events.title: Legacy RPC status, error, method, and service attributes are deprecated
events.detail: Protocol-specific RPC attributes and older naming patterns are replaced by the more unified RPC model; peer.service is also deprecated in favor of service.peer.name.

events.title: Core RPC, gRPC, and Dubbo conventions reach release candidate
events.detail: The three RPC convention groups are promoted to release candidate. The release also removes older RPC network attributes.

events.title: JVM metrics become stable
events.detail: The JVM metric conventions reach stable, while TLS/SSL conventions and deprecations continue to evolve around them.

events.title: CPython runtime metrics are introduced
events.detail: The Python runtime surface grows with CPython-specific runtime metrics, alongside additional runtime and profiling coverage.

events.title: Kubernetes attributes are explicitly marked alpha
events.detail: Kubernetes attribute conventions are labeled alpha in the release, making their maturity visible rather than implicit.

events.title: Selected Kubernetes and container registry attributes stabilize
events.detail: A selection of Kubernetes and container registry attributes is promoted to stable. This does not make all Kubernetes conventions stable; selected memory metrics reach release candidate in v1.44.0.

events.title: CPU mode, process attributes, and core CPU metrics reach release candidate
events.detail: Several system and process surfaces are promoted to release candidate, showing maturity advancing in parallel across neighboring domains.

events.title: Process namespace, Kubernetes memory, and interface naming reach release candidate
events.detail: The latest release promotes process namespace, Kubernetes container memory, and network.interface.name conventions to release candidate.

events.title: Messaging gains Kafka metric conventions
events.detail: Kafka metrics are added as an early specialized messaging surface, before the messaging model is later generalized and reshaped.

events.title: Experimental Kafka metrics are removed
events.detail: The experimental Kafka metric conventions are removed rather than carried forward unchanged, an example of release history that is not simply additive.

events.title: Messaging operations and metric names are generalized
events.detail: Generic messaging operations and metric renames reshape the messaging conventions, reducing dependence on one protocol’s vocabulary.

events.title: Version-control-system metrics are introduced
events.detail: VCS metrics enter the semantic-conventions surface, followed by resource conventions and continued repository metadata refinement.

events.title: CI/CD and VCS resource conventions arrive
events.detail: The release adds CI/CD resources and spans plus VCS resources, extending the timeline beyond runtime telemetry into delivery and software lifecycle systems.

events.title: CI/CD and VCS conventions reach release candidate
events.detail: CI/CD, VCS, and process-related convention groups are promoted to release candidate in the same release wave.

events.title: Messaging operation spans and Kafka cluster identity are updated
events.detail: The latest release adds messaging operation spans and Kafka cluster identity, continuing the move toward more expressive operation-level conventions.

events.title: JavaScript runtime and CloudEvents conventions appear
events.detail: JavaScript runtime conventions and CloudEvents are introduced, making runtime and event-driven application behavior visible in the model.

events.title: GraphQL semantic conventions are introduced
events.detail: GraphQL joins the growing set of protocol and application-specific convention areas.

events.title: Feature-flag conventions are introduced
events.detail: Feature-flag evaluation becomes a first-class event-oriented convention area.

events.title: Profiling semantic conventions are introduced
events.detail: Profile conventions enter the repository, expanding the model beyond traces, metrics, logs, and resources.

events.title: CLI and geographic conventions are introduced
events.detail: The CLI span and geo attribute groups are added as compact, reusable convention components.

events.title: Browser web-vital conventions arrive
events.detail: Browser web-vital conventions are introduced as a specialized signal surface, later reworked in v1.44.0.

events.title: browser.document is introduced
events.detail: The browser surface gains a document-oriented convention, complementing the earlier web-vital work.

events.title: Browser web-vital conventions are reworked
events.detail: The latest release records a breaking rewrite of browser web-vital conventions, illustrating why the timeline needs an explicit update category in addition to stability.

events.title: Generative-AI client conventions are introduced
events.detail: A dedicated gen_ai client surface enters the core repository, starting a fast-moving domain that later gets its own repository.

events.title: gen_ai.prompt and gen_ai.completion are deprecated
events.detail: The initial prompt/completion approach is deprecated in favor of log-based events, a migration from span-oriented data toward richer event records.

events.title: Older GenAI response-format conventions are deprecated
events.detail: The GenAI model continues to evolve: older response-format choices are deprecated as output-type conventions are introduced.

events.title: GenAI chat history is reworked
events.detail: The chat-history model is revised and older message-event forms are deprecated, another compatibility transition inside the still-experimental domain.

events.title: Core gen_ai conventions are deprecated and moved to a dedicated repository
events.detail: All gen_ai.* conventions are deprecated in the core repository as the GenAI work moves to its dedicated semantic-conventions repository. This is a repository migration, not the end of GenAI conventions.

events.title: HTTP client and server conventions enter the specification
events.detail: HTTP client and server span conventions move from working drafts into the main OpenTelemetry specification. HTTP material was already imported on 13 May 2019; this milestone dates entry into the main spec, not the invention of HTTP telemetry.

events.title: Database client conventions enter the specification
events.detail: Database client span conventions move from the working draft into the main specification, including db.type, db.instance, db.statement, and db.user. The draft was imported on 13 May 2019; the displayed interval starts at entry into the main spec.

events.title: gRPC conventions enter the specification
events.detail: gRPC client/server span and message-event conventions move into the main specification. A gRPC draft was imported on 13 May 2019. General RPC conventions follow on 17 June 2020; this is the gRPC origin, not an assertion that generic RPC was already defined.

events.title: Messaging span conventions enter the specification
events.detail: A dedicated messaging-system convention defines spans and messaging.* attributes for systems such as Kafka, RabbitMQ, and ActiveMQ. Earlier imported OpenTracing material described message_bus.destination and producer/consumer spans; this dates the OpenTelemetry messaging convention, not the first messaging tracing concept.

events.title: Kubernetes resource conventions enter the specification
events.detail: Kubernetes resource labels enter the main specification, including cluster, namespace, pod, and deployment names. These build on OpenCensus resource conventions already imported as working material on 13 May 2019. The origin concerns resource attributes, not Kubernetes metrics.

events.title: JVM memory metrics are added
events.detail: The changelog records JVM memory runtime conventions in v1.9.0. This starts the selected memory-to-stability history, not all JVM telemetry history.

events.title: JVM CPU metrics are added
events.detail: CPU metrics expand the JVM conventions before stabilization.

events.title: Browser attributes are introduced
events.detail: The browser.* attributes appear in v1.12.0; web vitals follow almost three years later.

events.title: Database attributes are renamed and deprecated
events.detail: db.statement becomes db.query.text; db.name becomes db.namespace; db.operation becomes db.operation.name. db.user is deprecated before the database core reaches release candidate.

events.title: RPC conventions extend beyond gRPC
events.detail: The specification adds common remote procedure call conventions, rpc.system and rpc.method, and support for non-gRPC systems. This extends the gRPC-specific conventions that entered the specification in June 2019.
